group_assessment.weighting: A Sydney neurolipid and neuroimmunology consortium (lipid mass-spectrometry, cytometry and electron-microscopy cores, from the contributions). Primary for CerS2 in myelinating cells; WWOX is absent. entries.proposition: The model deletes CerS2 (exons 2-11 flanked) in myelinating cells with CNP-Cre; WWOX is not in the paper.
entries.snippet: To delete CerS2 in myelinating cells, mice homozygous for the floxed CerS2 allele (CerS2fl/fl) were bred to mice with heterozygous expression of Cre recombinase from the CNP gene locus (CNP‐Cre) (Lappe‐Siefke et al., 2003)
entries.anchor: Methods, conditional knockout mice

entries.proposition: Untargeted brain lipidomics at 6 weeks: 532 lipids quantified, 107 differing at q below 0.01, led by HexCer and sulfatide species with chains over 20 carbons falling and C16-C18 HexCer rising.
entries.snippet: A total of 532 phospholipids, sphingolipids, and neutral lipids were identified, based on both precursor and product ions, and quantified relative to internal standards (Supplementary Table 1). Of these, 20% (107) were differentially expressed between CerS2fl/fl and CerS2ΔO/ΔO mice at a false discovery rate‐adjusted p value of .01
entries.anchor: Results, myelin lipid acyl chain length

entries.proposition: Table 2: ST(d18:1_24:1) is 49,891 in controls and 1,288 in the knockout (units are those of the untargeted run); the C18 hexosylceramide rises about 3.9-fold.
entries.anchor: Table 2, row 2

entries.proposition: Table 2: Hex1Cer(d18:1_18:0) rises from 3,213.54 to 12,544.07.
entries.anchor: Table 2

entries.proposition: The deposited Table S1 reproduces Table 2 for the lipid ST(d18:1_24:1): means 49,891.33 (6 controls) and 1,287.83 (7 knockouts).
entries.anchor: Supplementary Table 1, derived by script from the deposited xlsx

entries.proposition: In purified myelin the very-long-chain species fall and C16-C18 species rise, and totals of HexCer, sulfatide and ceramide rise while total sphingomyelin is unchanged: chain length, not sphingolipid amount, is the change.
entries.snippet: Increased C16‐C18 variants produced an increase in total HexCer, ST and ceramide in myelin from CerS2ΔO/ΔO relative to CerS2fl/fl mice, despite reduced C22‐C24 variants (Figure 3f–h), whereas total SM was not significantly different (Figure 3i).
entries.anchor: Results, myelin lipid acyl chain length

entries.proposition: Myelin cholesterol content is unchanged between genotypes.
entries.snippet: Myelin cholesterol content did not differ between CerS2fl/fl and CerS2ΔO/ΔO mice (1577 ± 202 vs. 1616 ± 140 nmoles/mg protein), and sphingolipid levels in the liver did not differ between the two genotypes (Figure 3k–n).
entries.anchor: Results, myelin lipid acyl chain length

entries.proposition: The increased C18 hexosylceramide is galactosylceramide (HILIC separation), made by oligodendrocytes.
entries.snippet: Using hydrophilic interaction (HILIC) chromatography we confirmed that the increased C18 HexCer content of both brain homogenates and purified myelin was GalCer, not GluCer.
entries.anchor: Results, myelin lipid acyl chain length

entries.proposition: Death starts at 14-16 weeks and affects 80 percent of the knockouts by 22 weeks; spontaneous tonic seizures were seen.
entries.snippet: In our initial characterization of CerS2ΔO/ΔO mice, sudden, unexpected deaths occurred, starting from 14–16 weeks of age and affecting 80% of the mice by 22 weeks (Figure 4a). Spontaneous tonic seizures were also observed in CerS2ΔO/ΔO mice.
entries.anchor: Results, myelin degeneration and early lethality

entries.proposition: Myelin loss and protein loss are absent at 6 weeks (except a small PLP reduction) and pronounced at 16 weeks.
entries.snippet: Myelin staining (Figure 4d) and protein levels (Figure 4e,f) were not reduced in CerS2ΔO/ΔO relative to CerS2fl/fl mice at 6 weeks of age, apart from a small reduction in total PLP content.
entries.anchor: Results, myelin degeneration and early lethality

entries.proposition: Heterozygous deletion in oligodendrocytes (dO/+) causes no myelin loss and a subtle balance-beam deficit only.
entries.snippet: No discernible loss of myelin (Figure 4m) or myelin protein markers (Figure 4n,o) was observed in 16‐week‐old mice heterozygous for CerS2 deletion in oligodendrocytes (CerS2ΔO/+).
entries.anchor: Results, myelin degeneration and early lethality

entries.proposition: At 6 weeks electron microscopy shows normal-appearing myelin but a lower percentage of myelinated axons and a higher g-ratio, three mice per group.
entries.snippet: However, quantitative analysis revealed a reduction in the percentage of myelinated axons (Figure 5c). Smaller‐caliber axons < 0.5 μm were particularly affected (Figure 5d).
entries.anchor: Results, reduced myelin thickness

entries.proposition: Mature oligodendrocyte density is unchanged at 6 and 10 weeks and reduced by 33 percent (corpus callosum) and 56 percent (striatum) at 16 weeks.
entries.snippet: By 16 weeks, mature oligodendrocyte density was 33% lower in the corpus callosum and 56% lower in the striatum of CerS2ΔO/ΔO mice, although unchanged in the cerebellum.
entries.anchor: Results, gliosis and axon stress

entries.proposition: A distinct microglial population (myelin-responsive microglia, TMEM119 and P2RY12 low, CD68, CD11c, MHC-II high) is about four-fold more abundant at 6 weeks and eight-fold at 10 weeks, from three mice per group.
entries.snippet: and was approximately 4‐fold more abundant in 6‐week‐old CerS2ΔO/ΔO compared to CerS2fl/fl mice, increasing to 8‐fold in 10‐week‐old CerS2ΔO/ΔO mice
entries.anchor: Results, phagocytic microglial population

entries.proposition: There was no lymphocyte infiltration and no change in monocyte, macrophage, T, B or NK cell numbers; a modest neutrophil increase was seen.
entries.snippet: We observed no significant lymphocyte infiltration in the brains of 6W or 10W CerS2ΔO/ΔO mice that might be suggestive of autoimmunity.
entries.anchor: Discussion

entries.proposition: Increased C16-C18 sphingolipid is attributed by the authors to higher dihydrosphingosine substrate, not to increased CerS1 or CerS6 protein; the CerS1 and CerS5 antibodies could not be validated.
entries.snippet: however we were unable to reliably identify a band at the expected size with one commercial CerS1 and two commercial CerS5 antibodies.
entries.anchor: Results, myelin lipid acyl chain length

entries.proposition: The authors state that earlier CerS2-null reports of HexCer loss reflected older white matter and that chain length, not GalCer and sulfatide loss, is sufficient to destabilise myelin; TREM2 sensing and the denatured-MBP epitope are named as untested possible triggers.
entries.snippet: Myelin phagocytosis by microglia can be initiated by interaction of the receptor TREM2 with myelin lipids such as ST and SM, when myelin or cellular debris is present
entries.anchor: Discussion, paragraph 9

entries.proposition: The cause of the sudden deaths was not determined.
entries.snippet: Death in CerS2ΔO/ΔO mice was sudden and unexpected. This necessitated modification of our ethics protocol such that CerS2ΔO/ΔO mice were only kept up to 4 months of age, and we were unable to determine the exact cause of death.
entries.anchor: Discussion, paragraph 8
